title_clean: 85 The Root of All Things — Mūlapariyāya Sutta (MN 1)
description_short: An introduction to the Buddha's most challenging discourse on how perception and conception create our sense of self and world through the four perversions.
description_long:
Bhante Bodhidhamma introduces the Mūlapariyāya Sutta (MN 1), considered one of the most difficult discourses in the Middle Length Discourses. Known as 'The Root of All Things,' this sutta reveals how we construct our sense of self and world through distorted perception and conception.

The talk explores the four perversions (vipallāsa) of perception: seeing the impermanent as permanent, the painful as pleasant, not-self as self, and the foul as beautiful. Bhante explains how from initial misperception, we develop concepts through wrong view, attachment, and conceit (māna), leading to four types of relationships with experience: identity, inclusion, separation, and ownership.

This systematic analysis shows how we build up our conceptual world and sense of self through multiple layers of misunderstanding. The discourse covers everything from the four elements in our body to various god-realms, jhāna states, sense objects, and even mistaken ideas about Nibbāna. Bhante recommends Bhikkhu Bodhi's detailed commentary for deeper study, noting this is just an introductory exploration of this profound teaching on the roots of suffering and delusion.
